page: Google Cloud Platform e2-small is an entry-level shared-core virtual machine categorized under the E2 family. It operates on the x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor, providing 2 vCPUs supported by a single physical core across two threads, with a fractional allocation equivalent to one-quarter of a physical core. The instance is provisioned with 2.0 GB of system memory (1.0 GB per core) and includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. It contains no dedicated hardware accelerators (0.0 GPUs) and includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results reflect the resource limits imposed by its fractional shared-core architecture. In computational testing, the instance scored 270.6 in stress-ng single-core and 355.5 in multi-core metrics, falling within the bottom 10 percent of recorded systems. PassMark metrics align with this profile, registering a CPU score of 521.28 and a memory score of 335.47. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 24.74 GB/sec, placing in the middle 50 percent, while memory bandwidth tests peaked at 11.3 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks but fell to 2.47 GB/sec read and 2.26 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks. Application tests showed static web serving throughput at 0.54 GB/sec and Redis SET performance at 0.18 million operations per second.

The primary operational tradeoff of e2-small is constrained throughput and burstable compute capacity in exchange for cost efficiency. The lack of bundled local disks, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and specialized instructions such as AVX-512 restricts its viability for sustained high-throughput workloads. This instance profile fits lightweight background services, low-traffic web endpoints, development testing, small microservices, and non-critical batch scripting that do not require continuous CPU engagement.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-small is a budget shared-core instance based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B12 processor. It provides 2 vCPUs backed by a fractional 0.25 physical core allocation and 2.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage, complimentary public IPv4 networking, and hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the lower tier for sustained compute and memory bandwidth, showing 355.5 in stress-ng multi-core and 521.28 in PassMark CPU, though it reaches average single-threaded throughput in gzip compression at 24.74 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 0.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.54 GB/sec static web throughput. Designed for cost-conscious deployments with light CPU demand, e2-small is suited for basic development environments, light background tasks, microservices, and low-volume web serving.
